title: Noon's descendants: Johnny Lane, Joe Marsala and Bob Gordon
summary: Noon's influence runs through Lane to Marsala and on to young Bob Gordon, whom Chace admires and who is about to go on the road with Muggsy Spanier.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Before we leave Noon entirely, I want to mention that several people were influenced into succeeding generations by Noon, according to their own testimony. Johnny Lane has spoken about Noon as being, in his mind, the model clarinet player. And if I remember correctly, Lane taught Joe Marsala.
Marsala, in turn, made a record of... Could have been... I know that you know.
I believe he did, yes. Which is very close to Noon. I don't have it. I wish I did. Very close to Noon.
So Marsala, as well, tried to emulate that.

So it might easily have extended through a couple of generations. Now, Marsala, in turn, has a new pupil, a fellow lately in town by the name of Bob Gordon, who is considerably respected. We'll watch and see if Noon, by any chance, gets all the way through to Gordon. That might happen.

Well, I certainly hope so. And I think there's a good chance of it, John. I know Gordon's playing, and I admire him enormously, although I resent and envy him. He's going to take my jobs away from me. He's 19. I think he's just turned 20. I don't know. He's going on the road with Muggsy Spanier next Monday, by the way. He adulates Marsala, and I think he has a great deal of the same lightness and deftness about his playing that Marsala showed. There's a sprightliness about Marsala's playing, never mind the tempo or the nature of the tune, that's quite unique. And as you say, it's going to be very interesting to watch this lineage as it expresses itself in Gordon's playing as the years go by.
